verdicts.why: Webflow sells extra seats with no headcount cap, and its Agency Workspace gives every client site its own free seats, where Framer's 10-seat cap applies to the whole workspace at once.
Neither tool can take a payment for a course or a download, so the actual sale still needs a separate checkout tool no matter which one builds the marketing site.
A real product catalog needs a dedicated back office with inventory and checkout: Framer has no cart at all, and Webflow's Ecommerce plans cap out at 15,000 items with a fee on the entry tier.
Framer's $15 Basic plan already includes a small CMS and its AI agents can draft a first site from a prompt, a faster, cheaper start than Webflow's design-first canvas.
Running several small client sites costs less on Framer, whose $15 Basic plan already includes a CMS, than on Webflow, where any site needing a blog has to move up to the $39 Premium plan.
A startup's marketing site can lean on Webflow's custom code and Webflow Cloud to host a small app alongside it, capabilities Framer's per-site plans have no equivalent for.
